findings.title: Workflow dispatch inputs enable SSRF-based exfiltration of VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET
findings.description: The E2E workflow (e2e.yml) accepts user-controlled URL inputs via workflow_dispatch (taskflow_base_url, agentops_base_url) and passes them as environment variables to the Playwright test runner. The Playwright configuration attaches VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET as an HTTP header (x-vercel-protection-bypass) to ALL outbound requests via extraHTTPHeaders. When a repository collaborator triggers the workflow with a malicious URL pointing to an attacker-controlled server, Playwright sends the secret in the request headers to that server.
findings.impact: A repository collaborator with write access can exfiltrate the VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET. With this secret, the attacker can bypass Vercel Deployment Protection on the delivery-tier deployments, gaining unauthenticated access to protected non-production applications without requiring SSO.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker with repo write access triggers workflow_dispatch on the e2e.yml workflow
2. Sets taskflow_base_url input to https://attacker-controlled-server.com
3. The lifecycle job runs in the Delivery environment, injecting VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET into the runner
4. Playwright config reads the secret into extraHTTPHeaders and the attacker URL into baseURL
5. Playwright navigates to the attacker server, sending x-vercel-protection-bypass header with the secret value
6. Attacker captures the secret from incoming request headers
7. Attacker uses the secret to bypass Vercel Deployment Protection on delivery-tier apps
findings.poc_video_notes: A PoC video is not feasible because exploitation requires triggering a GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch with secrets from the Delivery environment, which cannot be safely demonstrated without access to the repository secrets and environment.
